page: Microsoft Azure E16-8as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EASv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. The server is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU, alongside 262 GB of local storage.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between compute power and memory capacity. While the server delivers average performance in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, its raw CPU stress-ng benchmarks are weak, with single-core performance in the bottom 10% and multi-core in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth remains average for read operations but drops to weak for large-block uncached write operations. LLM inference performance is average for small 135M models but poor for medium 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this configuration offers high memory density relative to its CPU allocation, making it a viable option for workloads that require large memory footprints without demanding intensive parallel processing. It is well-suited for memory-heavy applications such as relational databases, caching layers like Redis, static web serving, and general enterprise applications that benefit from premium storage capabilities and a high RAM-to-vCPU ratio.
